observations: Blind Driving Assists expose position, orientation, braking, turn, and track-limit information through configurable audio cues.
Cue pitch and volume can be configured independently rather than treating accessibility as one global mode.
The feature set coexists with broader driving assists and input configuration.
inferences: Equivalent access may require different information channels rather than identical presentation.
Independent settings need combination testing because a valid cue can be masked or contradicted by another configuration.
limits: Official documentation describes available behavior but does not prove equivalence for every player or setting combination.
Latency and reward identity require direct instrumented testing.
